Table 3 presents regression results of our tests examining the relation between target firms’ financial


statement comparability and the efficiency of acquisition decisions: model (1) uses _ACQ_CAR_ (acquirer’s three

day announcement returns); model (2) uses SYNERGY (three-day value-weighted returns of acquirer and target);


and model (3) uses ∆ ROA (change in ROA from the pre- to post-acquisition period).


Using the three-day announcement period abnormal returns of the acquirer as the measure of


acquisition efficiency, the coefficient on target comparability is positive (0.017) and statistically significant at


the 5 percent level ( t -stat = 2.04) after controlling for acquirer, target, and deal characteristics. These results


support our first hypothesis that acquirers’ announcement returns are positively related to the pre-acquisition


level of targets’ financial statement comparability. In terms of economic significance, the acquirers’ three-day


announcement returns for targets that exhibit higher financial statement comparability are, on average, 1.7


percent higher than for targets that exhibit less financial statement comparability. <sup>21</sup> The model (1) results also


indicate that the market’s assessment of the quality of the acquisition as reflected in the acquirer’s three-day


announcement period abnormal return is significantly positively related to acquirer’s Tobin’s Q and leverage.

HYPOTHESIS 1a. Target firms’ pre-acquisition financial statement comparability is positively related to

acquirer abnormal returns around acquisition announcements.

HYPOTHESIS 1b. Target firms’ pre-acquisition financial statement comparability is positively related to

expected synergies from business combinations.

HYPOTHESIS 1c. Target firms’ pre-acquisition financial statement comparability is positively related to

post-acquisition operating performance of the acquirer.

Table 3 presents regression results of our tests examining the relation between target firms’ financial


statement comparability and the efficiency of acquisition decisions: model (1) uses _ACQ_CAR_ (acquirer’s three

day announcement returns); model (2) uses SYNERGY (three-day value-weighted returns of acquirer and target);


and model (3) uses ∆ ROA (change in ROA from the pre- to post-acquisition period).


Using the three-day announcement period abnormal returns of the acquirer as the measure of


acquisition efficiency, the coefficient on target comparability is positive (0.017) and statistically significant at


the 5 percent level ( t -stat = 2.04) after controlling for acquirer, target, and deal characteristics. These results


support our first hypothesis that acquirers’ announcement returns are positively related to the pre-acquisition


level of targets’ financial statement comparability. In terms of economic significance, the acquirers’ three-day


announcement returns for targets that exhibit higher financial statement comparability are, on average, 1.7


percent higher than for targets that exhibit less financial statement comparability. <sup>21</sup> The model (1) results also


indicate that the market’s assessment of the quality of the acquisition as reflected in the acquirer’s three-day


announcement period abnormal return is significantly positively related to acquirer’s Tobin’s Q and leverage.

Table 3 presents regression results of our tests examining the relation between target firms’ financial


statement comparability and the efficiency of acquisition decisions: model (1) uses _ACQ_CAR_ (acquirer’s three

day announcement returns); model (2) uses SYNERGY (three-day value-weighted returns of acquirer and target);


and model (3) uses ∆ ROA (change in ROA from the pre- to post-acquisition period).


Using the three-day announcement period abnormal returns of the acquirer as the measure of


acquisition efficiency, the coefficient on target comparability is positive (0.017) and statistically significant at


the 5 percent level ( t -stat = 2.04) after controlling for acquirer, target, and deal characteristics. These results


support our first hypothesis that acquirers’ announcement returns are positively related to the pre-acquisition


level of targets’ financial statement comparability. In terms of economic significance, the acquirers’ three-day


announcement returns for targets that exhibit higher financial statement comparability are, on average, 1.7


percent higher than for targets that exhibit less financial statement comparability. <sup>21</sup> The model (1) results also


indicate that the market’s assessment of the quality of the acquisition as reflected in the acquirer’s three-day


announcement period abnormal return is significantly positively related to acquirer’s Tobin’s Q and leverage.
